none: Meâl and a question only; this segment gives no explanatory claim.
Meâl only, followed by a transition to the next discussion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He allows that the promise may refer to the second recurrence of corruption mentioned earlier in the surah.
rows.anchor: sûrenin başında geçen وَعْدُ الْكَ َّرةِ الآْخِرَةِ yani ikinci kerreki fesâdın vadesi mânasına olmak melhuz ise de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Considering the promise that Israel would repeat its transgression and God would repeat punishment, he prefers the promise of the afterlife, meaning the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وَإِنْ عُدتُّمْ عُدْنَا mazmûnuna nâzır olarak وَعْدُ الْدَارِ الآْخِرَةِ mânasına olmak tekrardan sâlim ve binâen‘aleyh daha zâhirdir. Ki kıyamet demek olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent the Quran with truth and it descended with truth, without corruption.
rows.anchor: Onu -Kur’ân’ı- hak ile indirdik ve hak ile indi yani hiç bozulmadan indirdiğimiz gibi bihakkın indi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's wording, meaning, and descent are all true, and it came to the Prophet through divine wisdom.
rows.anchor: nazmı da hak mânası da hak, inişi de hak indiği de haktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's reports will certainly come to pass.
rows.anchor: Onun haber verdikleri muhakkak olacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger announces reward to the obedient and punishment to disbelievers and rebels.
rows.anchor: iman ve itaat edenlere sevâbı ve kâfirlere, âsîlere ikābı haber vereceksin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not charged with fulfilling everyone's wishes or forcing obstinate unbelievers to believe; he must carry out his warning and glad tidings without fearing the outcome.
rows.anchor: yoksa herkesin istediğini yapacak, anûd kâfirlere zorla iman verip kurtaracak değilsin.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mission of warning and glad tidings must continue; it is not completed in one instance.
rows.anchor: o tebşir ve inzar bir defada bitecek değil, tâkip olunmak lâzımdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran was divided into portions so the Prophet could recite it slowly and at intervals.
rows.anchor: ağır ağır, vakit vakit nâsa kıraat edesin için Biz onu ayırt

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its revelation was gradual, from foundational principles toward subsidiary matters, matching people's needs and circumstances rather than arriving all at once.
rows.anchor: hepsini birden değil, usûlden fürû‘a doğru nâsın her türlü mesâlih ve ihtiyâcâtına ve ahvâlin muktezayâtına mutabık olmak üzere tedrîcen indirdik.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a section, a tenth, or sometimes a single verse can stand as a complete lesson containing glad tidings and warning.
rows.anchor: bir hizib veya bir aşır ve hatta bazen bir âyet müstakil bir kitap gibi başlı başına tebşir ve inzârı muhtevî bir derstir.

rows.speaker: Ömer
rows.claim: A report attributed to Umar says to learn the Quran five verses at a time because Gabriel revealed it in fives.
rows.anchor: Ömer radıyallâhu anh’tan şöyle dediğini tahric etmiştir: ‘Kur’ân’ı beşer âyet beşer âyet ta‘allüm ediniz.

rows.speaker: Ebû Sa‘îd-i Hudrî
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id reportedly taught five verses morning and evening and said Gabriel revealed the Quran in groups of five.
rows.anchor: Ebû Sa‘îd-i Hudrî bize Kur’ân’ı sabah beş ve akşam beş âyet tâlim eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although sound evidence establishes revelations of more and fewer than five verses, the reports mean that five-at-a-time was usual.
rows.anchor: beşten daha fazla ve daha az olarak nüzûlünün vâki‘olduğu da sahîhen sâbit bulunduğundan murad, ekseriya demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether opponents believe the Quran does not affect its truth or perfection; belief benefits them and disbelief harms them.
rows.anchor: İnanmanız onun kemâlini artırmaz, inanmamanız da ona nakīsa vermez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given knowledge earlier were scholars who studied prior scriptures and understood revelation, religion, law, and proofs of prophethood.
rows.anchor: kütüb-i sâlifeyi tedkik etmiş olup da vahyin, kitabın, din ve şeriatın ne olduğunu anlamış, delâil-i nübüvvete vâkıf olmuş değerli âlimler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their praise means the Prophet promised in earlier books has arrived and their other prophecies will occur.
rows.anchor: evvelki kitaplarda vaad ettiği O Peygamber geldi, haber verdikleri hep olacaktır diye tesbih ve şükrediyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recitation makes these knowledgeable people weep and increases their humility.
rows.anchor: -Kur’an okundukça- onların huşû‘larını artırıyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites as a parallel people whose eyes overflow with tears when they hear revelation and recognize the truth.
rows.anchor: تَرَىٰٓ أَعْيُنَهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ ٱلدَّمْعِ مِمَّا عَرَفُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet prayed in Mecca using both Allah and Rahman, polytheists accused him of worshipping two gods, and this command was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: “yâ Allah yâ Rahmân” diye dua ederken müşrikler işitmişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah's beautiful names express the highest beauty, majesty, and generosity, and prayer using any of them is permissible.
rows.anchor: En yüksek cemâl ve celâl ve ikram ifade eden Esmâ-i Hüsnâ hep O’nundur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having many names does not entail multiple named beings; invoking all the beautiful names is still prayer to the one God without partner.
rows.anchor: ismin ta‘addüdünden müsemmânın ta‘addüdü lâzım gelmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer recitation or supplication should not be shouted, lest it suggest ostentation or disrespect.
rows.anchor: namazda kıraat veya dua ederken bağırma; gösteriş, saygısızlık şâibesi olmasın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It should not be so quiet that one cannot hear oneself, as though afraid of others; the right way is between the extremes.
rows.anchor: işitmeyecek kadar da gizleme, mâsivâdan korkuyormuş gibi olmasın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has no child by begetting or adoption; those claiming otherwise fail to know His majesty and lie.
rows.anchor: doğurmaktan münezzeh olduğu gibi evlâtlık da edinmedi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Claims that two or three beings share God's kingdom are false; He has no partner in sovereignty.
rows.anchor: ona mülkte şerîk yok iki veya üç diyenler, başkalarını karıştıranlar iftira ettiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no ally to escape humiliation or gain honor; although He loves and grants friendship to righteous servants, He befriends none from need.
rows.anchor: herhangi bir ihtiyaçtan dolayı dost edindiği hiçbir velî de yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is inherently mighty and should be magnified in essence, attributes, acts, and names.
rows.anchor: Zâtında da büyükle, sıfâtında da büyükle, ef‘âlinde de büyükle, esmâsında da büyükle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet reportedly taught this verse to each son of Abdulmuttalib as soon as he began speaking and called it the Verse of Might.
rows.anchor: Abdulmuttalib evlâdından söylemeye başlayan her oğlan çocuğuna Resûl-i Ekrem işbu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's close with praise and magnification fittingly follows its opening with glorification and the Night Journey.
rows.anchor: Tesbih ve İsrâ ile başlayan bu sûrenin bu آيَةُ الْعِزّ’de hamd ü tekbir emirleriyle hitâmı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing praise and magnification are specially connected to the great favor promised to the Prophet in 17:87.
rows.anchor: nimetine şüphesiz bir terettüb-i mahsûsu vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet recited this surah and Surah al-Zumar every night.
rows.anchor: bu sûre ile Sûre-i Zümer’i her gece okurdu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports the Prophet called this surah and the following ones among his earliest treasures and old possessions, meaning early Meccan revelations and treasured memorized devotions.
rows.anchor: İbn Mes‘ud’dan rivayet olunduğu üzere Resûl-i Ekrem bu sûre ile bunu tâkip eden Kehf, Meryem, Tâ-Hâ, Enbiyâ sûreleri hakkında buyurmuştur ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the sequence from Isra's promise of the Praised Station to Anbiya's declaration that Muhammad was sent as mercy as deliberately ordered on that basis.
rows.anchor: tebcîline müntehî olan Sûre-i Enbiyâ’ya kadar bu beş sûrenin tertîbi de bu esas üzeredir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next surah's opening praise harmonizes with Isra ending in praise and magnification.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Kehf’in hamd ile başlaması ne ahenkdârdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent the Book without crookedness: it is straight, authoritative, and free of falsehood or error.
rows.anchor: dolambaçlı değil, çarpık değil, yalanı yanlışı yok

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book warns of a very severe punishment from God, namely the punishment of the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: pek şiddetli bir azab olan âhiret azâbını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It promises a beautiful reward to believers who do good works, and they will remain in it forever.
rows.anchor: onlara öyle güzel bir ecir muhakkak ki onda ebediyen kalacaklar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning addresses Arab polytheists who call angels God's daughters, Jews who call Uzayr His son, and Christians who call Messiah His son; Christians insist most because it is their first doctrine.
rows.anchor: “Allah’ın kızları” diyen Arab müşrikleri, Üzeyr’e “Allah’ın oğlu” diyen Yehûd, “Mesih Allah’ın oğlu” diyen Nasârâ’dır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither the claimants nor their forebears know this doctrine; they repeat it from ignorance and imitation, although knowledge rejects it.
rows.anchor: bunu söyleyenler bildiklerinden değil bilmediklerinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God a child-bearer is a grave audacity and major sin, a huge utterance from their mouths.
rows.anchor: Allah’a karşı büyük bir cür’et, azîm bir kebîre olan büyük bir laf oldu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terms ‘fathers’ and ‘word’ evoke Christian terminology and signal that this claim especially grows on Christian lips, though commentators have not noted the allusion.
rows.anchor: tâbirlerinin Nasârâ ıstılâhından olduğuna dikkat edilirse bu kelimenin en ziyade onların ağzından çıktığına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes the Christian fathers' repeated claim that a voice from heaven said the Messiah was God's son, and calls it a lie.
rows.anchor: Âbâ-yı Nasârâ “‘Mesih oğlumdur’ diye semâdan bir ses geldi” derler dururlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is nearly exhausting himself with grief that these people reject the new Book and may perish unbelieving.
rows.anchor: bu hadîse, yani bu yeni kitaba inanmazlarsa sen arkalarından esef ile hemen hemen kendini tüketeceksin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is told not to grieve but to perform his duty and praise God who revealed the Book, since the liars will be ruined.
rows.anchor: sen onlara esef etme, gam yeme de sana bu kitabı indiren Allah’a hamd ederek îfâ-yı vazife et

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made earthly adornments a trial for believers and unbelievers, manifesting through their deeds who acts best, then rewarding good and punishing evil.
rows.anchor: mü’min ve gayr-i mü’min insanları mübtelâ kılalım, hangisi amelen daha güzel imtihan edelim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Today's dazzling adornments will soon become dust and ruin; true good action serves their everlasting Creator rather than clinging to temporary beauty.
rows.anchor: Bugün gözler kamaştıran o ziynetler, yarın bakarsın dünden yokmuş gibi harâb ü türâb olup gidecek.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should not waste time grieving over what will perish, but strive for the best deeds in this testing ground.
rows.anchor: o helâk olacaklara esef ile üzülmemeli, vakit geçirmemeli de bu imtihan meydanında en güzel amele çalışmalıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kahf means a mountain cave, especially a large one as distinct from the smaller ghar; its Turkish equivalent is in.
rows.anchor: dağda mağara ve bilhassa geniş olanı ki küçüğüne “gār” denilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raqim means an inscribed tablet made of stone, metal, or another material.
rows.anchor: yazılı taş veya maden veya sâireden levha demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Companions of the Cave and Inscription are not an exceptional marvel beside divine power that adorns the earth, tests people, destroys worldly beauty, and grants eternal reward for good deeds.
rows.anchor: Ashâb-ı Kehf ve Rakīm tek bir acîbe, şaşılacak bir âyet mi oldular sandın? Hayır, bunda şaşılacak bir şey yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings astonishing signs and excellent deeds from tested people who do not become deceived by worldly life; He has done and will do many greater things.
rows.anchor: en şâyân-ı hayret alâmetleri sonu türab olan dünya ziynetine, dünya hayâtına aldanmayan mübtelâlar içinden izhar etmek âdet-i ilâhiyedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although others may be amazed, the Prophet should remember he has witnessed greater signs and is expected to produce better deeds.
rows.anchor: taaccüb etseler de daha büyük âyetlere mazhar ve daha güzel amel kendisinden matlub olan sen

none: This segment consists of verse translations only; no separate explanatory claims are given.
This segment consists of verse translations only; no separate explanatory claims are given.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nawf al-Bikali reportedly claimed that the Musa who accompanied Khidr was not the Israelite Musa; Ibn Abbas angrily rejected him and cited the Prophet to identify him as the familiar Moses.
rows.anchor: sâhib-i Hızır olan Mûsâ, sâhib-i Benî İsrâil olan Mûsâ değil zu‘munda bulunuyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's Musa cannot be understood as anyone other than the well-known Moses son of Imran.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’da zikrolunan Mûsâ’dan diğer bir Mûsâ anlaşılamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most reports identify Moses' young attendant as Joshua son of Nun, who served and learned from him; calling a servant fata was literary Arabic usage because servants were usually young.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ’nın fetâsı, yani delikanlısı da ekser rivayete göre Yûşa‘b. Nûn’dur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith instructs people not to call servants ‘my male or female slave’ but to call them fata.
rows.anchor: hizmetçilerinize ‘kölem’, ‘cariyem’ demeyiniz, ‘fetâm’ deyiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although another attendant is possible, sound reports name Joshua, placing the journey after the Exodus in the wilderness of Tih.
rows.anchor: ahbâr-ı sahîhada Yûşa‘vârid olmuştur. O hâlde vak‘a Mısır’dan hurûcdan sonra sahrâ-yı Tîh’te iken vukū‘bulmuş demek olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a report, God says His most beloved servant remembers Him and does not forget Him; the wisest rules by truth without desire, and the most learned seeks others' knowledge in hope of guidance or rescue.
rows.anchor: buyurulmuş ki: “Beni zikreden ve unutmayan”.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After learning someone was more learned, Moses asks to find him and is directed to the meeting of the two seas, where he will lose the fish.
rows.anchor: mecme‘u’l-bahreyn’de, sahrânın yanında balığı gayb edeceğin yerde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ka'b al-Qurazi identifies the meeting of the seas as Tangier, the Strait of Ceuta.
rows.anchor: Ka‘b-i Kurazî’den Tanca, yani Sebte boğazı olduğu rivayet edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ubayy reportedly places the meeting of the seas in Ifriqiya.
rows.anchor: Übey’den de İfrîkiye[^11] olduğu menkuldür.

rows.speaker: Mücâhid ve Katâde
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatadah reportedly identify the place as the meeting of the Persian and Roman seas.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid ve Katâde’den Bahr-i Fâris ile Bahr-i Rum’un mültekāsı diye rivayet olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That view would require an isthmus, not a strait; he suggests the land between the Indian Ocean and Mediterranean where the Suez Canal was later cut.
rows.anchor: Bahr-i Muhît-i Hindî ile Akdeniz arasında Süveyş kanalının açıldığı bir berzah olsa gerektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He considers Jerusalem's well-known Rock a likely referent for the rock mentioned with the meeting place.
rows.anchor: Kudüs’teki mâruf Sahratullah olmak çok muhtemildir.

rows.speaker: İbn Atıyye
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the Persian Sea is a branch of the Indian Ocean reaching north to south in Persia, locating the confluence where the seas meet the lands of Syria.
rows.anchor: İbn Atıyye demiştir ki: “O, yani Bahr-i Fâris Bahr-i Muhît’ten bir koldur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes take bahreyn as the dual ‘two seas’ and overlook Bahrain as a proper name; dictionaries describe it as a region between Basra and Oman on the Indian Ocean coast.
rows.anchor: bir ism-i hâs olmasını nazar-ı itibara almamış görünüyorlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Bahrain is a place name, the meeting place could mean the center or seat of the region, a clearer reading and nearer than Ceuta.
rows.anchor: Bahreyn kıt‘asının toplu yeri veya makarrı demek olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A journey to Bahrain after Moses' earlier travel to Midian is not implausible, though exegetes give no transmitted support for this reading.
rows.anchor: Daha evvel Medyen’e gitmiş olan Mûsâ’nın ba‘dehû Bahreyn’e bir seyahati de müsteb‘ad değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes may avoid the proper-name reading because the next verse uses a dual pronoun, although some refer that pronoun to Moses and his companion.
rows.anchor: bundan sonraki âyette tesniye zamiri ile مَجْمَعَ بَيْنِهِمَا buyurulmuş olmasıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views take the seas as salt and fresh water, or as the Kurr and Ress rivers near Azerbaijan.
rows.anchor: bazıları da Azerbaycan tarafındaki Kürr ve Ress nehirleri olduğunu söylemiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret the meeting as the two seas of knowledge, Moses and Khidr; al-Kashshaf calls it innovative, Abu Hayyan likens it to Batini interpretation, and many reject it.
rows.anchor: iki ilim denizi demek olan Mûsâ ile Hızır’ın ictimâ‘ettikleri mahal demektir diyenler olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although literally remote, this interpretation is semantically sound: the text definitively indicates the place where Moses and Khidr meet.
rows.anchor: bu mâna lafzen ba‘îd olmakla beraber meâlen sâbittir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He flags the addition of ‘between’ in ‘meeting between them’ rather than simply ‘their meeting’ as a rhetorical point.
rows.anchor: buyurulmayıp da araya bir de “beyn” ilave edilmiş olmasının nüktesi düşünülmelidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses forgot to ask about the fish and his attendant forgot to report it; the fish was their food, so it had been dead before the miracle.
rows.anchor: Siyaktan anlaşılıyor ki Mûsâ sormayı unuttu, fetâsı da söylemeyi unuttu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead fish taking a path through the sea exemplifies resurrection; because Moses did not know it, it was a miracle for the sought-after servant, while the attendant saw it and forgot to tell him.
rows.anchor: demek ki ölülerin dirilmesine numune olan bir mucize vukū‘bulmuştu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although other exegetes infer a seashore rock, he argues that the phrase most naturally means Jerusalem's known Rock; a waterhole could explain the fish entering the sea there.
rows.anchor: Fakat biz bunun Kudüs’teki mâruf Sahra olduğuna hükmetmek istiyoruz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The travelers went a considerable distance from the Rock before reaching the boat; the episode may also preserve the origin of the Rock's sacred status.
rows.anchor: gemiye bininceye kadar hayli gitmiş olduklarına nazaran

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attendant says Satan made him forget to mention the fish, which seemed impossible to forget given its extraordinary path through the sea.
rows.anchor: Onu söylememi bana her hâlde Şeytan unutturdu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final y of nebghi is omitted despite analogy; the licensed omission is more eloquent and implies the search had ended.
rows.anchor: fakat alâ hilâfi’l-kıyas olarak yâ hazfedilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another recitation retains the final y.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh yâ ile kıraat da vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They retraced their steps to return to the place they had passed.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh izlerini tâkip ederek geri döndüler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mercy granted to the servant means the gift of revelation and prophethood.
rows.anchor: vahiy ve nübüvvet nimetiyle mütena‘‘im kılmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes identify the servant as Khidr; Sufis citing reports not authenticated by hadith scholars say he never died and sometimes appears, and some interpret mercy as long life.
rows.anchor: Hızır’ın hiç vefat etmediğine ve bazen görüldüğüne kāildirler.

rows.speaker: Nevevî
rows.claim: Ibn Salah and Nawawi reportedly cite the consensus of spiritual masters that Khidr is alive, though the claim has been challenged.
rows.anchor: Nevevî gibi bazı zevât-ı fihâm, Hızır’ın hayatı hakkında meşâyihin icmâ‘ını nakletmişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many scholars, including the exegetical majority according to Abu Hayyan, hold Khidr died; they cite hadith and 21:34, and usually interpret this mercy as revelation and prophethood.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân bunun cumhur kavli olduğunu kaydetmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qayyim says all hadiths asserting Khidr's life are fabricated and none is sound.
rows.anchor: hayatı hakkında sahih bir hadis bile yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi concludes sound Prophetic reports and strong rational premises fully support those who say Khidr died, with no reason to abandon apparent meanings.
rows.anchor: vefat etti diyenlerin kavline tamamıyla müsaid ve davalarını tamamıyla müeyyiddir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says stories whose authenticity God alone knows and esteem for Sufi authorities such as Ibn Arabi do not constitute evidence for Khidr's life.
rows.anchor: bu da bir delil teşkil etmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi advises weighing both sides' proofs and consulting one's heart rather than accepting a claim merely because of its proponent's stature.
rows.anchor: tarafeynin delillerine ve leh ve aleyhindekilere vukuftan sonra kalbinden istiftâ et

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi cautions against condemning those who disagree with Sufis on the question, while saying Sufis too reject claims refuted by law or reason.
rows.anchor: Sakın birtakımlarının yaptığı gibi bir hususta sûfiyyeye muhalefet edeni hemen tadlîle kalkışma.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For outward physical life, he finds the scholars who say Khidr died plainly correct, citing 3:144 and 5:75 as sufficient evidence.
rows.anchor: reddeden ulemânın kavli zâhir olduğunda şüphe yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sufi symbolic speech should not be debated only according to its outward wording; the Moses and Khidr story has outward and inward dimensions.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ ve Hızır kıssası bir zâhir ve bâtın kıssası olduğuna göre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Konevi says Khidr exists in the imaginal realm; Kashani identifies Khidr with expansion and Elijah with contraction; others define Khidr-ness as a spiritual rank reached by righteous people.
rows.anchor: Şeyh Sadrüddin İshak Konevî Tebsıratu’l-mübtedî ve tezkiretü’l-müntehî nâmındaki eserinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He accepts these three Sufi formulations as a key to understanding the issue.
rows.anchor: bu üç sözü meselenin miftâhı olmak üzere kabul edebiliriz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ledun is an adverb like ‘with’; min ladunna means ‘from Our presence’ or ‘from Our side,’ and qualifies the teaching rather than knowledge, though divine teaching may entail divinely given knowledge.
rows.anchor: “Ledün”, “inde” gibi bir zarftır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All prophetic knowledge is ledunni as divinely taught revelation, but the verse marks Khidr's instruction as a special knowledge unlike Moses' and belonging to hidden sciences.
rows.anchor: Şüphe yok ki bütün enbiyânın ilmi taraf-ı ilâhîden vahy ü tâlim olmak itibariyle ledünnîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes explain Khidr's knowledge as knowledge of the unseen and hidden secrets; Moses knew law and outward adjudication, whereas Khidr knew inner realities.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ’nın ilmi ma‘rifet-i ahkâm ve zâhir ile iftâ, Hızır’ın ilmi ise, bevâtın-ı umûra marifet idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a Bukhari report, Khidr says each has knowledge taught by God that the other does not know.
rows.anchor: ben Allah’ın ilminden bana tâlim ettiği bir ilim üzereyim ki, sen onu bilmezsin.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ledunni knowledge in its narrower technical sense is also called knowledge of reality or the inward, and Sufis use this story as evidence for it.
rows.anchor: buna ilm-i hakikat ve ilm-i bâtın dahi denilmiş ve sûfiyye, bu kıssaya bir hüccet olarak tutunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ledunni knowledge cannot be gained through intellectual effort; it is a pure divine gift and direct disclosure, with reality impressed upon the soul rather than inferred from effects.
rows.anchor: taraf-ı Hak’tan mevhibe-i mahza olan bir kuvve-i kudsiyenin tecellîsidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Turkish, ‘the ledunniyat of a matter’ means its hidden intricacies and secrets; the story encourages seeking knowledge and travel while showing this special knowledge cannot be acquired by effort.
rows.anchor: bâtınındaki gavâmız ve esrârı mânasında müte‘âreftir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rüşd means attaining good; Moses' request teaches humility toward a scholar, right guidance as learning's chief aim, and the need for deference, courtesy, following, and service.
rows.anchor: “Rüşd” hayra isabet demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr's prediction displays his first insight into Moses' spirit, later vindicated; Moses' lesson is to recognize his station and learn patience amid hidden acts that outwardly seem wrong.
rows.anchor: Fi’l-hakīka bu talepte Mûsâ’nın alacağı ders kendi makamını tanımak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a law-bearing prophet, Moses would feel compelled to object to actions whose hidden wisdom he could not grasp and which looked wrong outwardly.
rows.anchor: Sen bir sâhib-şeriat olmak haysiyetiyle onları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses promises patience and obedience while qualifying his promise with God's will.
rows.anchor: “beni” dedi, “inşaallah sabırlı bulacaksın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr forbids questions until he explains matters himself, including debate, objection, and even inquiry; unlike other disciplines where questioning is half of learning, this study prepares receptivity over agency.
rows.anchor: münakaşa, itiraz şöyle dursun, istifsâren sual bile sorma.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They immediately set out, showing that this knowledge is learned through events rather than sitting, conversation, or reflection.
rows.anchor: bir yerde oturup söyleşmek veya düşünmek tarîkiyle değil, fi‘liyyât ile bellenecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attendant is no longer mentioned because he was subordinate to Moses and perhaps was left somewhere behind.
rows.anchor: O, Mûsâ’nın tâbi‘i olduğu için artık kāle alınmamış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abi Hatim through Rabi ibn Anas says the place was frightening, the sailors distrusted the travelers and hesitated, but the captain saw their radiant faces and admitted them.
rows.anchor: Rebî‘b. Enes’ten rivayetine göre mevki korkunç idi, gemiciler bunlardan şüphelendiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says the sailors recognized Khidr and carried them without charging a fare.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan rivayetinde ise Hızır’ı tanıdılar, navılsız bindirdiler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reports describe the boat damage as an ordinary operation with an axe or adze; perhaps the sailors stayed quiet because they knew Khidr.
rows.anchor: keser veya balta gibi âlât

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The style and the sailors' silence better suit a miraculous hole made quietly.
rows.anchor: bir hârika şeklinde sessizce yapılıvermiş olması daha mülâyimdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes take ghulam to mean a child not yet at puberty; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz that he was twenty, and the word can also mean a young man.
rows.anchor: cumhur bunun henüz bâliğ olmamış bir çocuk olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Moses meant the killing was unlawful and that denial of a retaliation right especially fit the context.
rows.anchor: murad, katlin bi-gayr-i hak olduğunu söylemektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Moses may imply that his law required retaliation even when the victim was a child.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ’nın şeriatında sabîye de kısas lâzım geldiğini iş‘ârdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses the final description as a thoroughly abhorrent deed.
rows.anchor: çok münker bir şey yaptın.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The village has been identified as Antioch, Ubulla, Barqa, Nazareth, Bacirvan, a village in Roman territory, or Algeciras; Antioch's name is later, so its earlier name would differ.
rows.anchor: birçokları Antakya olduğunu söylemiş. “Antakya” ismi müteahhir olduğuna göre eski ismi başka olmak lâzım gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The village cannot be reliably identified; since the Quran does not require its name, it leaves the place indefinite and describes its relevant trait instead.
rows.anchor: bu karyenin mevsûkan tâyini kābil değildir. Esasen Kur’an’da tâyini matlub olmadığından nekre gösterilip yalnız şöyle bir vasfı anlatılmıştır:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated word ‘people’ may distinguish the governing body from the general residents; if both mean the same inhabitants, the repetition intensifies the reproach.
rows.anchor: “ehl”in iki defa zikrolunması birisi şehrin asıl hükûmeti, biri de umum ahâlisi olmak gibi iki mânaya işaret olsa gerektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All ranks of the population were so base as to refuse hospitality to two travelers.
rows.anchor: bu karyenin havâss u avâmıyla bütün ahâlisi o kadar alçak imişler ki iki kişiyi misafir etmekten çekinmişler.
